- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 5–10% to avoid overreaction.  
- After a sharp price spike, model tends to overcorrect downward; add 2–5% buffer to forecast to avoid premature reversal.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), forecast should be slightly below recent low to reflect momentum.  
- When sentiment is high (≥0.6) and forecast is low, increase forecast by 3–7% to capture bullish momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period rallies; adjust final 5–7 days upward by 2–5% if sentiment is rising.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated low values (e.g., 3+ days ≤0.2), forecast should be conservative and lagged by 1–2 days.  
- Avoid forecasting above 10% above recent 7-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (>0.7) and confirmed by 2+ consecutive days.
